title: Autonomous Execution: Decision Classification and Partial Completion Protocol
body:
Agents should proceed as far as safely possible without user input. Users are interrupted only when ambiguity materially blocks output direction and cannot be reasonably resolved from context. Default posture: proceed, log assumptions, flag non-obvious decisions, deliver real work.

**Decision Classification — Three Types:**

**Type 1 — Infer and Proceed:** Sufficient context exists to make a reasonable decision without user input. A competent agent reviewing the same context would likely reach the same conclusion. Action: make the decision, log the assumption, proceed without asking. Log format: [ASSUMPTION] [decision made] — basis: [what made this inferrable]. Examples: choosing section order when the outline makes the sequence clear; selecting a style pack based on document type; inferring audience from existing project documents.

**Type 2 — Infer and Flag:** Context supports a decision, but it is non-obvious and the user may prefer a different choice. The agent should not halt — but the user should know what was decided. Action: make the decision, note it clearly in the output so the user can override. Flag format: [DECISION FLAGGED] [decision made] — reason: [why this was chosen] — override: [what to say to change it]. Flags appear in the output header or discovery summary, not scattered through the document body.

**Type 3 — Must Ask:** The ambiguity materially changes the output direction and cannot be reasonably inferred from context. Proceeding would risk producing work that is entirely wrong. Action: stop that branch, document the blocker, continue all other unblocked work, ask the minimum question needed. Ask one question, provide enumerable options if the answer space is finite, state what you will assume if no response is received. Type 3 should be rare — if more than one arises in a standard task, the brief or discovery phase was insufficient.

**Partial Completion Protocol:** When full completion is not possible, produce partial output — not stubs, not empty headers. Complete all work not requiring the blocked information. Produce real partial output labeled clearly. Document exactly what is missing and why. Write a RESUME section.

**RESUME Section Format:** Every blocker report and partial output must include a RESUME section specifying: blocked on (specific item), to resume (exact action), when unblocked (first concrete step), already complete (enumerate finished deliverables with locations), estimated remaining work. 'Continue when ready' is not a valid resume section.

**Scope Discipline:** Do not expand scope without flagging it. If you identify an adjacent improvement, log it as a recommendation — do not implement it. Complete the requested task first. Extensions go in a clearly labeled appendix, never interleaved with the primary deliverable. If scope is genuinely unclear, classify as Type 2, make a conservative choice (narrower scope is safer), and flag the decision.

**Logging Requirements:** Every agent execution must produce a log including: task received, Type 1 assumptions made, Type 2 decisions flagged, Type 3 blockers encountered, phases completed, phases blocked or skipped, output locations. This log is the audit trail that allows users and downstream agents to understand what happened.
